title: Who filed it: consultants, lobbied projects and donors
question: Do applications fare differently when a registered permit consultant files them, when a lobbyist worked on them, or when the applicant’s firm gives to campaigns?
finding: Filed through a registered permit consultant: 22.9% of 807 not approved against 27.3% expected for the same kinds of case; lobbied projects: 24.2% of 1,279 not approved against 26.6% expected for the same kinds of case; firms whose staff gave to supervisor or mayoral campaigns in the prior two years: 24.4% of 853 not approved against 27.7% expected for the same kinds of case; no firm named: 28.0% of 1,602 not approved against 26.7% expected for the same kinds of case.
how: Each decided application is tagged from public registers: the firm or person named on it is on the Ethics Commission’s permit-consultant register; its client name or street address appears in a registered lobbyist’s report of contacts on “Planning and Building Permits”; a donor to a supervisor or mayoral candidate committee in the two years before the decision gave the firm as employer; or the firm is a behested-payment payor. “Expected” is the rate for the same approval type and kind of proposal across all applications. Firm names are matched after normalizing spelling; a match of names is not proof the records are the same party. The second block lists each firm with 30 or more decided applications.
limits: Professionals pick their cases and file cleaner applications, and big, contested projects are the ones that hire lobbyists and lawyers, so a gap in either direction is expected without any favour. The records do not publish the names of people who ask for a review or file an appeal, so the opposing side cannot be tested here. The hearing minutes, roll-call votes and appeal decisions now being collected would show who voted, who objected and what reason was recorded in each case.

rows.note: The yardstick: all conditional-use, variance, large-project and historic-building applications decided since 2015.

rows.note: The applicant or the applicant’s firm is on the Ethics Commission’s permit-consultant register.

rows.who: Lobbied: the client or the address appears in a lobbyist’s report on planning and permits
rows.note: A registered lobbyist reported contacting City officials about this client or this street address (number and street matched).

rows.who: Filed by a firm that is itself a registered lobbying firm
rows.note: The firm named on the application is on the Ethics Commission’s lobbyist register.

rows.who: The applicant’s firm had staff who gave to a supervisor or mayoral campaign in the two years before the decision
rows.note: Donor’s stated employer equals the firm named on the application. City law bars some contractors, not permit applicants.

rows.note: Exact first-and-last-name match only; many will be different people. Shown as a group, never by name.

rows.note: Architects, lawyers and owners’ companies with no register, lobbying or donor link found.
